annotations.text: TOP BAR — ~10 controls + 2 readouts crammed into a 52px strip that already wraps. The active dataset is shown three ways: the seg, the '◦ luminal-a' text, and (in compare) the vs-picker.
PANEL TOGGLES are scattered — rail + inspector sit in the top bar, trace tree sits in the toolbar. Three show/hide toggles, two regions, no grouping.
MODE is two Figtree-600 pills (.pill). Every other mode control in the app — Focus, Direction — is a mono segmented control. Two idioms for the same job.
COMPARE is fragmented: mode pill (top bar), vs-picker (top bar), Compare-by + specific/differential/common + synced badge (toolbar). Turning it on touches three places.
TOOLBAR — four unlabelled categories in one wrap row: subgraph query · canvas display · comparison · panel toggle. Under wrap the groups scramble.
TOP BAR now carries identity · dataset · mode only. Dataset shown once. Mode is a segmented control — the same idiom as Focus and Direction.
VIEW cluster gathers every show/hide + reset behind one label, one idiom (toolbar-pill). A middle dot splits panels (rail·inspector·trace tree) from canvas overlays (labels·info band·minimap).
Hairline vertical rules mark the toolbar's cluster boundaries, so the groups stay legible when the row wraps. 'search & jump' is dimmed until it is wired.

COMPARE mode: the vs-picker drops out of the top bar into a single COMPARE cluster with the metric picker, the specific/differential/common state and the synced badge — every compare control in one place, shown only while compare is on.
VARIANT: the VIEW cluster collapses to one 'view ▾' popover — the tightest toolbar, at the cost of one extra click per toggle. Weigh against Main's always-visible cluster.
